newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge reduces life term for pizza thief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge reduces life term for pizza thief.

text.p: A man sentenced to life in prison for stealing a slice of pizza will walk free in two years following a judge's ruling that could undermine California's so-called "three strikes, you're out" law.
"I was real pleased because this was a classic case that illustrated the excesses of the three-strike law," attorney Arnold Lester said on Wednesday.
The court-appointed lawyer for Jerry Williams was reacting to a ruling on Tuesday by a judge in suburban Torrance which dramatically reduced Williams' prison term.
At a hearing, Judge Donald Pitts said his action was based on new sentencing discretion given judges under a three-strikes ruling by the California Surpeme Court.
Under the formula, Williams will be freed in little more than two years.
In March 1995, Pitts sentenced Williams to 25 years-to-life for snatching a slice of pizza from four children on the Redondo Beach pier.
He already had previous convictions for robbery and drug possession, and under the "three-strikes" state law aimed at punishing habitual criminals, he received the life sentence.
In his ruling on Tuesday, Pitts said that neither the crime nor Williams' history merited a life behind bars.

"Judge Pitts did the right thing," attorney Lester told local KCAL television. "He (Williams) knows he got his life back. He intends not to bother people again and understands it was a stupid thing he did."
The ruling is certain to have implications on the whole "three-strikes" law.
There was no immediate comment from state Attorney General Dan Lungren, a strong advocate of the law, or from the Los Angeles District Attorney Gil Garcetti.
